chunks: And that which was narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): regarding

the person in ihram who forgets and clips a nail from his fingernails, he said: 'He gives charity with a handful of food.' I said: 'And for two?' He said: 'Two handfuls.' I said: 'And for three?' He said: 'Three handfuls, every nail is a handful until it becomes five. If he clips five, then upon him is one blood [fine], whether it was five or ten or whatever it was.' For it does not contradict what we mentioned, because in the report it is not stated that if he clips five, upon him is blood without adding anything to it. So if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as meaning that when he adds to it the nails of the other hand, by the indication of the preceding report from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). And this expiation only binds the one who clips his nails intentionally, and does not bind the one who does so by way of forgetfulness. Indicating that is what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood fine (a specific type of sacrificial offering)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for clipping nails while in ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates the graduated expiation for intentionally clipping nails while in ihram, establishing that each nail incurs a handful of food until five are clipped, at which point a blood fine (dam) is due. He reconciles this with reports of exemption for forgetfulness by distinguishing between deliberate transgression and accidental error, a nuance supported by the preceding narration from Abu Basir regarding the accumulation of nails from both hands.
